name: The Barrow Heart
description:
Beyond the door lies a round chamber cut from the living rock, its ceiling lost in shadow. Ash lies ankle-deep on the floor, undisturbed except for a single path of footprints: armored, heavy, walking a slow circle around the room, again and again and again.

At the center stands a stone sarcophagus carved with a knight at rest, hands folded over a sword.
revisit: Ash, stone, and silence. The sarcophagus dominates the Barrow Heart.

variants.text: On the lid, where the knight's hands meet, sits an iron lantern with no light in it.
Ser Halric lies on the sarcophagus lid with his gauntlets folded over his sword, as still as his effigy. The circle of footprints in the ash is already beginning to blur.
Shattered bones and rusted plate lie scattered across the ash where Ser Halric fell.
The Barrowlight waits on the sarcophagus lid.
Beside the sarcophagus, a spiral stair yawns open in the floor, leading down into the deep earth.

ambient: The ash on the floor stirs, though there is no wind.
You hear the faint creak of armor that isn't yours.
The cold here goes all the way to the bone.

exits.description: The bronze door leads back to the Ossuary Hall.

features.name: sarcophagus
features.description: The effigy on the lid wears the flame of the Ashen Order on its shield. An inscription runs around the base: HALRIC OF THE ASHEN ORDER, WHO KEEPS THE LIGHT UNTIL HE IS RELIEVED.

features.name: Barrowlight
features.description: An iron lantern, plain and heavy, its glass smoked black. When you lean close you feel the faintest warmth, like an ember buried deep in ash.

interactions.label: Take the Barrowlight
interactions.text:
You lift the lantern from the sarcophagus, and at your touch the old ember inside it catches. Light spills across the Barrow Heart, pushing the shadows back into the stone.

Then the floor shudders. Deep beneath the sarcophagus, stone grinds on stone, slow and enormous, like a mechanism that has waited centuries for this weight to leave the lid. The base of the tomb slides aside to reveal a narrow spiral stair cut into the bedrock. Warm air breathes up out of it, smelling of wet earth and spores and lit faintly from somewhere far below, and with it comes the distant chime of a bell.

then.text: In your hand, the Barrowlight's flame settles into a warm, steady gold, as if it remembers the mercy that freed it.

else.text: In your hand, the Barrowlight's flame settles into a thin, ash-pale glow, as if it remembers the steel that won it.

features.name: spiral stair
features.description: Where the base of the sarcophagus shifted aside, a worn spiral stair winds down into a cavern far deeper than any hilltop barrow has a right to be. Far below, pale lanterns glimmer through a mist of ash and silver moss.

interactions.label: Descend the spiral stair into the Under-Barrow
interactions.text: You hold the Barrowlight high. Its flame leans toward the depths like a compass needle pulling home, and you step onto the descending stair.

then.text: At every turning you chalk the Ashen flame on the wall. Far above, faint and steady, Sister Wren's footsteps follow you down.

encounter.intro:
The lid of the sarcophagus grinds aside. A figure in rust-red plate sits up, then stands, ash pouring from the joints of its armor. Behind it, something thin and hungry claws its way up out of the ash on the floor.

"Who comes to relieve the watch?" the knight rasps. "No one. No one ever comes."

Its blade comes up.

options.label: Tell him his watch is over
Name the vow he keeps, and the one you broke
Speak to him as one dead thing to another

onSuccess.text: The knight's sword lowers by inches. "Relieved," it whispers, as if tasting the word. "At last." The thrall slumps back into the ash it came from. Ser Halric climbs onto the sarcophagus, folds his gauntlets over his sword, and is still.

onFailure.text: "Lies," the knight hisses. "They always lie." Its grip tightens on its blade.

onVictory.text: Ser Halric falls to his knees, then falls apart. His helm rolls across the ash and comes to rest facing the lantern he guarded for so long.
